answer: Use proof-of-unique-latency vouching by timed challenges. At registration, three random verifiers each send a fresh nonce to the new agent's network endpoint and require a signed reply within a tight round-trip bound. The registry records the measured delay triple as a location fingerprint and caps how many identities may share one fingerprint, such as a willow-lined inlet of one datacenter rack. Beyond the cap, additional keys earn zero voting weight, so an orchard of fakes must rent distinct hosts in different regions, roughly five dollars monthly per identity.
